To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nitro-heteroaromatic antimicrobial drugs are metabolized by a reductive pathway in micro-organisms, that the target of action is DNA, and that the spectrum of activity of the drugs is determined by the reducibility of the drugs by different species.
the antibacterial action of MEV is due to its activation by micro-organism to a DNA damaging agent.

the antimicrobial activity of nitro-hydroxy-imidazoles is due to their activation to a reactive species by the action of oxygen-labile enzymes, that these enzymes are inducible by the drugs and that the inducibility is related to the antimicrobial activity and the spectrum of activity of the drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of a group of antimicrobial drugs, namely the nitro-heterocylics, and with the factors that influence their antibacterial activity.
the metabolism of nitroheterocycles by micro-organisms and the role of the products in the mechanism of action of these drugs.
the mechanism of action and metabolic activation of nitro-hetorocyclic antimicrobial agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nitroimidazols and nitrofuranes are reduced to the corresponding hydroxylamines which are the active species.
the mechanism of action of MEV and related nitro-hetero- cyclic compounds is metabolic activation by the target cell to form a reactive metabolite which then reacts with DNA.
the antimicrobial activity of the nitroheterocycles is due to their metabolic activation by micro- organisms, and the spectrum of the drugs is related to their reduci-bility by different species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nitro-hetercyclic drugs are activated by the same mechanism in different species, but that the rate of activation is dependent on the reducibility of the drugs and that the spectrum of antimicrobial activity of the drugs is related to their reducitibility.
the antibacterial activity of nitroimidazolyl drugs is related to their metabolic reduction.
the mechanism of action of the nitro-heteroaromatic antimicrobial drugs involves the reduction of the drugs by the micro-organisms to form highly reactive intermediates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antimicrobial drugs that are not activated by microorganisms in vitro can be activated by microorganisms grown in oxygen-limited environments.
antimicrobial drugs that are not activated by the host may have reduced toxicity and that the toxicity of antimicrobial drugs may be related to the ability of the host to metabolize them.
the antimicrobial spectrum of nitro-hetrocyclic drugs appears to be related to the rate of their reduction by different species and the metabolic activation of the drug.
